claims.meaning: Adjusts approach based on context; comfortable with pivot and iteration. Stabilized by reads room tension before people speak; adjusts based on perceived dynamics. Primary (flex) drives forward movement. Secondary (signal) provides stabilization. Friction emerges when systems conflict. Action-focused perception, thorough processing, near-term focus. World experienced through flex lens. Model: . Speed: unknown.

3 domains: relational, infrastructure, energy. Primary: Moderate-High - Under stress, attention to people disappears; damage done without awareness. Team experiences flexibility as primary organizing force. flexibility-first communication structure shapes relational dynamics. Scaling constraint not identified.

Under pressure: Under strain, flexibility decreases; retreats to familiar patterns. Secondary system: Under strain, attention to people increases; can create hesitation. Normal operating → pressure applied → primary intensifies → secondary compensates or overrides. Build explicit decisive direction check-ins BEFORE pressure escalates Recognize when flexibility is amplifying — create circuit breakers Post-conflict repair: consciously re-engage decisive direction and pace after stress passes

Needs dimension refinement for specific role fit More than one role configuration can work; this is a demand-level map, not a job-title prescription. Hybrid - Can build or optimize depending on context Balanced - Can operate and envision Producer - Personal production primary Pragmatic - Explores when needed, stabilizes when required Balanced executor-strategist Moderate - Can handle ambiguity with boundaries Needs dimension refinement for specific role fit Executive Leadership Client-Facing/Relationship Management Process Management

Processes thoroughly, prioritizes accuracy over speed. Adjusts approach based on context; comfortable with pivot and iteration Decisions form through balanced assessment of options. Near-term time horizon—focuses on immediate next steps and short cycles. Moderate risk calibration—situational assessment drives risk decisions.

High-touch client relationships Consensus-required team cultures Direct communication culture, tolerance for bluntness Strengths remain assets at current scale Moderate-High - Under stress, relational awareness disappears; damage done without awareness Low - Direction stable Low - Execution reliable Moderate - Relational friction drains energy; isolation increases over time Low - Operates collaboratively The available governed source does not establish a longitudinal personal-energy trajectory.

domain_nodes.mission: Determine whether qualified opportunity supply is sufficient for the stated goals and how the operator actually creates it across a governed source portfolio.
domain_nodes.state_label: The operator reports insufficient current opportunity generation. SOI contact and local networking are available lanes; other named lanes are intentions rather than evidenced engines. Current evidence cannot separate generation scarcity from capture, qualification, follow-up, or market effects.

domain_nodes.mission: Locate where governed opportunity is captured, contacted, nurtured, qualified, appointed, presented, agreed, transacted and returned to relationship value—or leaks.

domain_nodes.mission: Determine whether recurring lead, client, listing, buyer, transaction and post-close work is produced by inspectable systems rather than memory or heroic effort.
domain_nodes.state_label: Listing, buyer, lead, transaction, and recruiting steps are articulated. The operator retains primary transaction follow-through while using coordinator support as needed. Operational repeatability is unverified despite the operator describing current processes as working.

domain_nodes.mission: Establish who owns which standards, how execution is inspected, how correction occurs and where accountability is absent or leader-dependent.
domain_nodes.state_label: Coaching is present for business development and recruiting. Routine business execution is primarily self-accountable or unowned. The operator attributes limitation to organization, time management, and distraction.

domain_nodes.mission: Reconcile what the business produces economically across units, volume, GCI/revenue, expenses, contribution, profit, cash, owner income and reinvestment capacity.
domain_nodes.state_label: Units, sales volume, gross, and expenses are reported for incompletely defined periods. Reported units and volume imply an average sale price below the separately stated average. Agent net, owner compensation, owner profit, cash, reserves, and contribution by source or closing are not established.

domain_nodes.mission: Determine present capacity, owner dependence, role/decision ownership, team economics and whether leverage is operationally/economically earned.
domain_nodes.state_label: Profit and business contribution are reported as equal while the operator reports performing most team work. The business partner participates in joint lead and client follow-up. No person-level team synthesis is authorized for the reported partner relationship.

domain_nodes.mission: Bind the present residential business model, desired operating future, strategic choices and goal economics so all other territories are interpreted relative to the business being built.
domain_nodes.state_label: The operator has explicit production, delegation, team, and office goals across multiple horizons. The reported current team pace is below the near-term monthly closing target. The growth plan lacks evidenced demand, economics, role, and process gates.

Evidence that would support the move: Workflow continuity persists across repeated cycles without hidden operator rescue. Released operator capacity is demonstrably redirected to relationship, system, or accountability work. Role and decision records support a clearer leverage-readiness judgment.

Evidence that would challenge the move: Nominal delegation leaves decisions and follow-through with the operator. Rescue work or quality failures expand. Operator capacity is neither released nor redirected.
Select one recurring workflow that currently returns to the operator.
Map its start, finish, standard, decision rights, exceptions, and evidence requirements.
Authorize controlled shadow-to-independent execution with operator involvement limited to defined exceptions.
Inspect commitments, outcomes, rescues, and intervention causes.
Retain, revise, or revert the transfer based on observed fidelity.
Pilot one workflow before extending the ownership model.
Predefine check-ins and escalation before workload pressure rises.
Treat the workflow as a seat-boundary test rather than proof of managerial readiness.

one_move.title: End-to-end ownership transfer trial
one_move.intervention: Transfer one recurring workflow with explicit decision rights, quality boundaries, exception rules, and inspected completion.
one_move.why_now: Requested organization, delegation, and team growth make transferability the immediate capacity question.
one_move.symptom_distinction: Tests transferable ownership rather than treating workload as a staffing-count problem or assuming equal economics proves misalignment.
causal_chain: Workflow boundaries make inputs, outputs, decisions, standards, and escalation explicit.
Role-level execution and rescue logging expose hidden dependence.
Independent completion releases operator capacity for constraint work.
Repeated evidence informs broader leverage readiness without requiring a hire.
assumptions: Operator-reported workload concentration is directionally reliable pending direct flow and time records.
An existing support role has enough capacity for a bounded trial.
Task volume is not treated as contribution value, and the current economic arrangement may be intentional or specialized.
prerequisites: Obtain explicit authority for the participating existing support role.
Select a recurring workflow that can be isolated without compromising continuity.
Define baseline queue, completion, interruption, rescue, quality, and decision records.
one_move.execution_definition: Complete after repeated end-to-end cycles are executed under assigned ownership and reviewed for quality, decisions, rescue, and operator intervention.
bounded_execution_steps: Select one recurring workflow that currently returns to the operator.
Map its start, finish, standard, decision rights, exceptions, and evidence requirements.
Authorize controlled shadow-to-independent execution with operator involvement limited to defined exceptions.
Inspect commitments, outcomes, rescues, and intervention causes.
Retain, revise, or revert the transfer based on observed fidelity.
one_move.owner_role: Operator owns scope, rights, standards, and exception decisions without silent rescue.

whole_person_execution_considerations.execution_adjustment: Pilot one workflow before extending the ownership model.
Predefine check-ins and escalation before workload pressure rises.
Treat the workflow as a seat-boundary test rather than proof of managerial readiness.

leading_indicators: End-to-end completions occur under assigned role ownership.
Operator decisions, interruptions, and rescues for the selected workflow become inspectable.
Quality and exception handling remain within defined boundaries.
success_evidence: Workflow continuity persists across repeated cycles without hidden operator rescue.
Released operator capacity is demonstrably redirected to relationship, system, or accountability work.
Role and decision records support a clearer leverage-readiness judgment.
failure_evidence: Nominal delegation leaves decisions and follow-through with the operator.
Rescue work or quality failures expand.
Operator capacity is neither released nor redirected.
falsifiers: Direct flow and time records show balanced ownership, stable execution, and no displaced constraint work.
